races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Em Four
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer for Saffie and Jamie Osborne who has shown ability on similar going (5/15 strike-rate, placed twice), but must generate momentum from the rear in a race where natural closers are overcrowded; 35 days off is a minor query.
runners_data.comment: Em Four brings distance and going experience to the table and, carrying 135 lb from stall five, his official mark of 74 looks workable against this field given our rating of 84 places him second among the six; the concern is that he has managed only one win in his last six starts, with three consecutive disappointing efforts since.

runners_data.name: Nogo's Dream
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners this six-year-old who has a solid record on Good ground (1W4P from 10 similar runs) and recent course form, but as a genuine hold-up type he faces the same crowded closing berth as Em Four and will need every stride of the run-in.
runners_data.comment: Nogo's Dream shaped well enough last time, finishing second, and has run over today's trip and going, giving connections plenty of confidence; yet to score in his last six starts, though our rating of 87 puts him narrowly top of this field and he carries 135 lb from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Olivia Haines's 7lb claim helps Stuart Williams's consistent five-year-old, who won over this exact trip on similar ground and boasts five places from seven comparable runs; a naturally prominent racing style means he is ideally suited to track Kento and challenge late.
runners_data.comment: Merrimack brings solid recent form to the table — a winner two starts back and placed third three starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while carrying 135 lb from stall two is the key question mark over his claims here.

runners_data.name: South Shore
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's five-year-old arrives on strong recent form (1122) and is a legitimate contender on ability, but his natural hold-up style — displaced toward midfield in the mapping because the field is heavy with closers — means he is likely to race a touch out of his comfort zone; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) tempers confidence in him producing his best in this shape.
runners_data.comment: South Shore arrives on the back of back-to-back runner-up finishes yet showed his quality with a win three starts back, and our rating of 75 gives him a solid claims; the main risk is whether he can convert placed efforts into victory under 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Raced just one day ago (LR:1d) which is the most pressing concern for John Gallagher's eight-year-old, who wears a visor and has two wins on this trip and going combination; his prominent style suits the race shape, but residual fatigue from a recent run on Good to Firm is a genuine physical query.
runners_data.comment: Ran just yesterday and faces a stiff ask on our figures as the lowest-ranked runner in the field, with an inconsistent recent profile — fifth last time out — though he has winning form in his last six starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old is the race's only confirmed front-runner and, fresh off a quick turnaround (LR:1d), will enjoy an uncontested lead under Ray Dawson; his pelham headgear helps him travel smoothly, and his recent placed form on Good ground keeps him dangerous if the pace is allowed to be gentle.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and trained by a yard that has had just one winner from 21 runners in the past fortnight, Kento is difficult to fancy despite his placing experience in recent starts and previous distance and going exposure, running just a day after his last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Kento is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner sprint and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead from the off, Ray Dawson should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop down the Brighton undulations. The two prominent types, Merrimack and Secret Handsheikh, will press for position just off Kento's shoulder, creating a race that unfolds at an honest but not breakneck pace — the kind that rewards those who travel well within the flow rather than those making up ground from far back. South Shore is a genuine hold-up horse displaced to a midfield mapping because this field contains more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Em Four and Nogo's Dream face the same challenge, meaning true off-the-pace tactics are compromised before the starter calls the field in. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured tempo — strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace comfortably and pounce in the final furlong, rather than hold-up horses forced to cover ground from wide or deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kento Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kento settles into a controlled lead and the prominent duo track without disruption, setting up a straight-line finish.
scenarios.body: Merrimack and Secret Handsheikh are ideally positioned to challenge as Kento's advantage is absorbed in the final furlong on the Good to Firm ground; their proximity to the pace means they spend no energy making up lengths and simply out-kick a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kento Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and Kento's rivals are slow to recognise the threat until it is too late.
scenarios.body: With a 7lb pull on most rivals and an uncontested lead, Kento can husband his resources perfectly and simply outstay the field on fast ground that suits a fresh, low-mileage sprinter; Ray Dawson, experienced at Brighton, could exploit hesitancy behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves stronger than anticipated and the prominent runners empty late, opening the door for closers.
scenarios.body: South Shore and Nogo's Dream would need a faster-than-expected tempo to generate momentum from off the pace, but South Shore's redistribution from its natural hold-up berth makes this a lower-probability outcome; a fast, strung-out finish is the only scenario that makes this viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses race out of role, the pace fragments, and no clear tactical advantage is established.
scenarios.body: Em Four and Nogo's Dream, both genuine closers forced forward, could benefit from a disorganised mid-race shape that scrambles positional advantages; however, with Brighton's camber favouring those nearest the pace at the two-furlong pole, a truly bunched finish without a clear pace beneficiary remains the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Kento's lead could prove unchallenged — watch whether Merrimack or Secret Handsheikh commit early enough to apply pressure, as a free-rolling front-runner on Good to Firm at Brighton is notoriously difficult to reel in once around the final bend.

Secret Handsheikh ran just one day ago; monitor his pre-race condition in the paddock — any sign of residual effort or lack of bloom could significantly reduce his chance of matching his usual prominent, forceful early foot.

South Shore is a natural closer being asked to race from a more forward position than ideal given the congestion of hold-up types; if he settles deeper than midfield he may simply run out of real estate over 5½f on a flat, fast surface.

Em Four and Nogo's Dream are both genuine hold-up horses competing for the same limited space at the rear — watch the early exchanges to see which rider concedes position and which, if either, manages to find a clear passage on the outside entering the straight.

Going is confirmed Good to Firm despite the race card listing Good — the faster surface marginally increases the premium on early position and favours those tracking Kento rather than those attempting to close.

races.name: Cognitive Law EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.note: Has moderate form (best a 4th) over 5-6f on comparable ground but has failed to win or place consistently; a genuine hold-up horse by nature whose effectiveness depends on being produced late, though in a small field with one relaxed pace-setter that run style faces a difficult task — style-fit concerns temper expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: I Am Royal
runners_data.note: OR of 120 signals strong stable confidence from Richard Hughes in what appears to be a debut or near-debut run; Billy Loughnane is a high-class booking but the unknown tactical profile on Good to Firm over 6f at Brighton leaves the actual race-day experience a complete wildcard.

runners_data.name: Major Looktwice
runners_data.note: Ran a respectable third on debut over this exact trip on Good ground, suggesting the step from experience to competition is already made; Tom Queally provides a patient front-end tactical option, and the matching trip and going profile makes this one of the more interesting open-market horses behind the pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Rogue Imperial
runners_data.note: Brighton's sole confirmed front-runner with four runs all on Good ground over 6f, posting two placed efforts from that sample; Archie Watson sends him here on 23 days' rest, and Harry Davies's booking is workmanlike — the key question is whether his sectionals will be strong enough to last the full trip without pressure forcing his hand early.

runners_data.name: Roll Up Raymond
runners_data.note: Finished third on debut over 6f on Good ground — identical conditions to today — for a small stable (T14: 0/3) that rarely pitches runners at meetings without purpose; Ray Dawson rides, and while the hold-up style suits a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate, the debut placed effort is an honest foundation.

runners_data.name: Happy Daisy
runners_data.note: Showed limited ability on debut (7th, 6f, Good) for Stuart Williams and arrives as the most exposed of the hold-up group; Marco Ghiani is an experienced Brighton pilot but the form offers little encouragement, and a rear-of-field hold-up run in a slowly-run small-field race on fast ground is a demanding brief.

races.paceDynamic: Rogue Imperial is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no meaningful pressure expected from rivals, should control a sustainable gallop from the outset over Brighton's undulating 6f on Good to Firm ground. The hold-up trio of From Me To You, Roll Up Raymond, and Happy Daisy will settle at the rear, though with three genuine hold-up types and only six runners, the race shape leaves the midfield largely vacated — creating a clean, unchallenged lead for Rogue Imperial who has form at this course and distance. Major Looktwice and I Am Royal are lightly raced unknowns whose tactical positioning remains fluid, but neither projects as a pace-pressing threat likely to force Rogue Imperial into a contested gallop. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: a lone leader controlling an honest but uncontested pace on fast ground over 6f is a textbook setup for a horse that can dictate and find more under pressure, with closers having to produce sustained finishing runs from further back than they would prefer. The field holds more hold-up types than can all find meaningful late cover — From Me To You is a genuine hold-up horse mapped here to midfield, but that redistribution signals the rear of the field will be crowded, making truly late runs from out of the pack less incisive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rogue Imperial Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Imperial leads unchallenged from the gate and sets a fair but measured tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Rogue Imperial dictates every yard, utilising his Good-ground course form at this trip to conserve energy and sprint clear entering the final furlong; the hold-up horses face too much ground to make up against a self-paced leader on fast ground. Prominent-position runners who track at close range benefit most if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Talent Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced-or-once-raced debutants (I Am Royal or Major Looktwice) produces an unexpected turn of foot to peg back the leader late.
scenarios.body: With high ORs of 120 suggesting significant stable expectation, either could be tactically placed just off the pace and produce a decisive late surge if Rogue Imperial's fractions are quicker than they appear; the fast ground and short straight suit a horse with a single sharp burst over a rival who has been in front too long. This scenario requires Rogue Imperial to have gone too hard early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a true finishing opportunity for a hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: From Me To You or Roll Up Raymond would need Rogue Imperial to press on hard from well back of the standard, exposing the leader in the final furlong; given the small field and lone front-runner dynamic, a truly strong pace is unlikely, making this scenario structurally improbable. Style-fit concerns for From Me To You (racing out of role) further reduce confidence in a late swooping finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Blows Race Apart
scenarios.trigger: If one or more rivals unexpectedly pressure Rogue Imperial from the front, turning this into a true pace battle.
scenarios.body: Should Major Looktwice or I Am Royal break sharply and contest the lead, the resulting strong gallop could see the front two tire simultaneously, gifting a fresher midfield or hold-up runner the race in the dying strides; this scenario is low probability given the absence of any second confirmed front-runner and the overall field size of just six.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Imperial's early sectionals are critical — if Harry Davies allows a soft lead through the first two furlongs he sets up an unassailable position; watch whether anyone pressures him jumping from the gates.

I Am Royal and Major Looktwice both carry OR 120 with minimal exposed form — either could be a well-prepared debutant with serious ability; watch paddock behaviour and market moves as the only reliable pre-race signal.

From Me To You has a style-fit concern in this race shape — mapped to midfield but a natural hold-up horse, watch whether Joe Leavy actually settles back or tries to position prominently to compensate, which would change the race dynamic.

The Good to Firm ground (confirmed by going report despite the stated Good) will put a premium on early pace and penalise horses who need time to warm into their stride — hold-up horses with slow burn finishes face a structural disadvantage on Brighton's sharp, undulating layout.

With only six runners and one clear pace-setter, the race is likely to be run in a near-perfect line without bunching — watch whether Roll Up Raymond or Happy Daisy can get a clean run from the rear, as traffic is unlikely to be an issue and finishing positions will be a true reflection of ability and tactics.

races.name: Ian Carnaby Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Von Krolock
runners_data.note: Won twice over 6f at Salisbury on Standard going and placed on Good, so conditions are squarely in range; Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is a meaningful weight advantage on a 7-year-old who knows how to win from a prominent pitch, and a six-day turnaround suggests the horse is in a productive run of form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom-two on our figures and rated below the official mark, Von Krolock is hard to fancy at the weights, though he does at least bring winning form into this, with a victory last time out and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Nordic Glory
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 6f on Firm and has the pace profile to slot in just behind Rye from a prominent position; Owen Lewis's 5lb claim helps offset the 24-day break, but the horse's mixed record on Good ground (1 from 15 in similar conditions) tempers confidence marginally.
runners_data.comment: Nordic Glory won last time out, which keeps him honest, but our figures rank him bottom of eight here and his recent form is patchy at best — that unplaced effort two starts back sits awkwardly alongside the win, and he is up against it on these ratings.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose best sim-going strike rate in the field (1W2P from 9 runs on Good) gives it solid credentials; the tongue-tie is notable, and Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim helps, though the horse must hope the pace stretches the field enough to generate a genuine finishing run.
runners_data.comment: Dark Sun arrives here in good heart after a third two starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going gives her a solid grounding; drawn in stall three and carrying 133 lb, she looks a genuine each-way contender on her overall profile.

runners_data.name: Rye
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who sets the tactical shape of the whole race, but an 80-day absence is a concern for a horse asked to do the donkey work from the front; the STYLE_FIT flag indicates it may not fully get its position, though it is listed as a confirmed pace-setter and Tony Carroll's 1-from-21 trainer form over 14 days adds little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last six starts, and a lengthy 80-day absence raises fitness questions, while her trainer's current 5% strike rate offers little encouragement; in her favour, she has experience over today's trip and going, and a second two starts back shows she can run her race.

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator whose recent form string (950088) is deeply uninspiring, and a 55-day break alongside a tongue-tie and visor combination suggests the connections are experimenting; the horse's best efforts came at longer trips and its Good-going record of 2W3P from 7 runs is decent but the recent profile is hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Blue Anthem carries top weight of 132 lb from stall one and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 64 putting him narrowly ahead — yet a winless run of six consecutive starts in recent form is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: The Organiser
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride on this 7-year-old whose natural finishing style makes him a true hold-up horse, but the redistribution means he is unlikely to get back as far as he'd prefer and his STYLE_FIT flag tempers his chance here; his best recent form has come over 7f on Good, so the 6f trip is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, The Organiser nevertheless arrives fit on a 19-day break, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 63 marks him as a genuine second-ranked threat from stall five; the risk is that elusive win continuing to evade him.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's 4-year-old has strong Good-going form (2W4P from 11 runs) and won over this exact trip and surface type, which is a genuine positive; however, the blinkers are back on and the horse's natural hold-up tendency means it finds itself mapped into a midfield role it won't naturally gravitate to, which is a real tactical limitation in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive sixth-place finishes in recent starts are the obvious concern, though she showed her best when scoring four starts back, with a second three starts back offering further encouragement; experience over today's trip and going, plus a 15-day turnaround, keep her in the mix from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Unico
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon's 5-year-old has been well beaten in recent starts (438-89) and the 76-day absence is notable; a genuine hold-up horse whose sim-going record (0W1P from 3) is thin on evidence, and the STYLE_FIT flag means the expected midfield berth rather than a deep hold-up position could cost it its best chance of a late finish.
runners_data.comment: Unico has experience over today's trip and going, and her third four starts back shows she can mix it at this level, but two consecutive eighths and a latest ninth suggest she arrives short of her best form after 76 days off — the fitness question is the main risk.

races.paceDynamic: Rye is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no significant challenger for the early lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop through the opening stages of this 6f Brighton sprint on Good to Firm ground. Von Krolock and Nordic Glory are the next two in the queue for prominent positions, and both should track comfortably just off Rye's shoulder rather than challenging for supremacy, meaning the pace is real but unlikely to be truly punishing. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely operate from the rear — The Organiser, Be An Angel, and Unico are true closers who are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield position rather than their preferred deep spot, compromising their ability to produce a sustained late run. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a measured gallop with two horses pressing from prominent positions — strongly favours horses racing in the P-to-M band who can travel smoothly and quicken in the final two furlongs without needing a strong pace collapse ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rye Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Rye sets a sustainable lead and the pace stays honest without collapse, allowing the prominent horses to strike from a close position.
scenarios.body: Rye bowls along at a comfortable clip on the Good to Firm surface, giving Von Krolock and Nordic Glory a clean tow into the race before the challengers make their move entering the final two furlongs. Prominent horses who can travel without cover and quicken off a steady pace are ideally served, and the measured gallop never generates the wall-of-pace that hold-up horses need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Rye goes too hard early and ties up in the final furlong, opening the race up for any horse finishing from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Rye, racing after an 80-day absence, could go too freely and empty inside the final furlong, causing the field to concertina and giving the deeper-lying horses a brief but real opportunity. Dark Sun, who has solid Good-going form over 6f and often finishes late, is best placed among the hold-up contingent to capitalise, though the redistributed runners — Be An Angel and The Organiser — are less likely to be far enough back to truly pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Redistributed Closers Caught Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is messy and the redistributed hold-up types find themselves trapped mid-pack without a clear run.
scenarios.body: The Organiser, Be An Angel, and Unico — all genuine closers pressed into midfield — risk getting caught in traffic on a track where Brighton's unique undulating finish rewards horses that find daylight early. If gaps don't open, their natural instinct to wait compounds the problem, and those already racing closer to the pace in a prominent position gain an unassailable advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Flees, Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rye bounces fresh after 80 days and simply bolts clear on a fast surface with no credible pursuer willing to apply pressure.
scenarios.body: A well-rested Rye finding the Good to Firm conditions to its liking could steal a march on a field that takes time to organise, building a lead that the shorter-priced prominent horses can never fully reel in. This scenario is narrow given the 80-day layoff and the presence of Von Krolock and Nordic Glory pressing from behind, but it cannot be entirely dismissed if Rye hits the ground running.

watchPoints.text: Rye's 80-day layoff is the pivotal unknown — if the absence has dulled its early pace or its handler lets it stride on too freely, the entire race shape unravels around the one horse meant to control it.

The three redistributed closers — The Organiser, Be An Angel, and Unico — are at genuine risk of crowding each other in midfield; watch for traffic issues and a scramble for the rail heading into Brighton's tricky closing stages.

Nordic Glory's mixed form on Good ground (1 win from 15 similar-going runs) may be masked by the prominent position it should enjoy — it could travel well and then not find enough in the final furlong on a surface that historically gives it trouble.

Dark Sun's tongue-tie is newly applied relative to some recent runs; if it settles better as a result and the pace holds, the horse's consistent Good-going placings (1W2P from 9) make it a quiet player from the hold-up group that could benefit most if the front end over-cooks the opening two furlongs.

races.name: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a win and two placings on similar going, but that run just three days ago is a significant concern — Jim & Suzi Best are 1/10 in the last 14 days suggesting steady rather than hot form, and this horse needs a truly run race to be seen to best effect.
runners_data.comment: Liberate shaped well on her latest start with a runner-up finish, and has run over today's trip and going, giving her strong claims as the top-rated runner in this field; the main risk is the quick three-day turnaround under a testing 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Bownder
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 48 days off for Jonathan Portman, whose recent 14-day record of 1/13 is lukewarm; the good-to-firm going is fine, but the lengthy layoff and limited similar-going wins (0W from 5) make confidence guarded even if the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Bownder has been consistently placed in recent starts, finishing second last time out and third in each of the two runs before that, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main concern is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Crimson Road
runners_data.note: Two wins from last three outings, both on good ground over 10 furlongs, mark her as the standout form horse here; William Carson rides and John & Rhys Flint are in decent touch (1/10 T14), though as a hold-up runner she needs traffic to part in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Crimson Road arrives in fine nick, winning two of his last five starts including back-to-back victories, and 15 days on from that latest success he lines up fresh and in-form, with experience of today's trip and going and a stall-one draw to note.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field, and Liam Wright (5lb claim) will be able to pop out and dictate unopposed; three wins and five places in similar going underline his affinity for fast ground, and a recent win 25 days ago means he arrives fresh enough to do it again.
runners_data.comment: Bobacious arrives on the back of a win, and his experience over today's trip and conditions is a clear asset carrying 135 lb from stall four; the main concern is that his recent record also includes a pair of disappointing finishes, suggesting he can be inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Star Mind
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is a genuine hold-up horse shuffled into the midfield map because the field is stacked with off-the-pace types; one win from 15 on similar going and an inconsistent form string (835180) make it hard to trust even if connections are 1/7 in the last fortnight.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but unplaced in each of her last two runs, Star Mind arrives here 18 days fresh and has run over today's trip and going, though her recent dip in form and a taxing 134 lb to carry from stall seven are clear hurdles to overcome.

runners_data.name: Bohemian Breeze
runners_data.note: Three wins in five recent starts, including back-to-back 10-furlong victories on good ground, represent the strongest recent form among the hold-up brigade; Tom Queally is an asset but this horse's natural style is closer/off-the-pace and it is forced to race in a more compressed midfield than ideal, which the 0.93 style-fit score reflects.
runners_data.comment: Bohemian Breeze has back-to-back wins two and three starts back, but fourth last time out tempers the momentum; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 133 lb from stall 8 makes this no straightforward task.

runners_data.name: It's Life
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR 56 and Billy Loughnane is a high-calibre booking, but this horse's last two runs were over 8 and 10 furlongs after a very long trip (18 furlongs) and the form is volatile; its natural rear-of-field style is compromised by the redistribution, tempering its claims.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, It's Life faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive in fair nick — a winner two starts back and runner-up last time out — with experience over today's trip and going, and 19 days between runs suggesting she is fresh.

runners_data.name: Twilight Guest
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 45 with a form string of 076446 that offers no encouragement; George Margarson is 0/6 in the last 14 days, and as a hold-up type forced into midfield, there is little here to suggest an upset is in the offing.
runners_data.comment: Twilight Guest has been winless in his last six starts, with a string of mid-pack and tail-end finishes offering little encouragement, and ranked last on our figures here he faces a stiff ask; the one mild positive is that he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Bobacious is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control fractions from the gates on Good To Firm ground over 1m2f at Brighton — a track that rewards horses able to dictate their own tempo. The pace is likely to be sustainable rather than frenetic, meaning Bobacious can roll along comfortably without being pressured into burning out early, which historically benefits the leader or a horse travelling just off them. Liberate, Crimson Road, and Bownder are the principal hold-up and prominent types, though Crimson Road's sharp recent form (two wins from last three) makes her the most dangerous closer if she can get a clear run from the rear. This race shape — a single uncontested leader on fast ground at a track that suits prominent racers — structurally favours the front-running and close-tracking profile; Bobacious sets it up, and anything hunting him down will need to travel sweetly through the race. Note: the field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Star Mind, Bohemian Breeze, It's Life, and Twilight Guest are all natural off-the-pace horses, but because the bulk of the field shares that style, several will be forced wider or into unnatural positions mid-pack, and only Bohemian Breeze (recent back-to-back wins) has the class to overcome that inconvenience.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bobacious Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious bowls along in front at a comfortable gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap on the Good To Firm surface.
scenarios.body: Bobacious sets an uncontested tempo, keeps something in reserve turning in, and the congested midfield of redistributed hold-up types cannot coordinate a clean challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Crimson Road Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If Crimson Road travels smoothly from off the pace and finds a clear passage to run down Bobacious in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Crimson Road's two recent wins and strong similar-going record (13/15) give her the raw form to reel in a solo leader who may flatten out late on a testing finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Bohemian Breeze Produces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bohemian Breeze, backed by three wins in five recent runs, produces a sustained finish from midfield once the field strings out.
scenarios.body: Despite being mapped out of role, Bohemian Breeze carries genuine class and back-to-back wins, and Tom Queally can manufacture a position if gaps appear over the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If early interference or a quicker-than-expected fractions shuffle disrupts the field order and the race is won by a horse producing a surprise late burst.
scenarios.body: An unlikely but non-zero shape where Liberate, It's Life, or Star Mind finds a clear passage as the race unravels; Star Mind's one win came with a dominant front-end effort and could be sparked if something tests Bobacious early.

watchPoints.text: Bobacious — if he gets to the front uncontested in the first furlong and sets a measured pace, he becomes very difficult to peg back on this flat Good To Firm track; watch whether any rider attempts to shadow him early.

Crimson Road — two wins in her last three and a dominant similar-going record mean she is the key danger, but watch the traffic situation in the straight: eight runners and a bunch of redistributed hold-up types in midfield could create a wall she cannot get through.

Bohemian Breeze — despite back-to-back wins, Tom Queally will have to work harder than normal to get a clean position given the horse's true hold-up style is being compromised by the race shape; watch whether he gets a clean outside run or is forced to wait too long.
Liberate — the three-day turnaround after a recent run is a notable flag; watch in the paddock and early strides for any signs of a horse that is not fully recovered from its last exertion.

Bownder — 48 days between runs combined with a lukewarm trainer strike rate warrants monitoring; if Olivia Tubb (5lb claim) settles her prominently and she travels well, she could outrun her odds, but fitness is the key unknown to watch through the early stages.

races.name: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dalmally
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator whose form figures of 8-5-8-6-3 show occasional ability to hit the frame over a mile on good ground; Thomas Greatrex rides for the modestly-striking Mark Pattinson yard (0/3 last 14 days) and 32 days off adds a small fitness query, though the OR of 55 gives a small class edge here.
runners_data.comment: Dalmally shaped with promise when third two starts back and steps up here on fitting distance and going experience, with our rating of 63 suggesting he holds strong claims from stall 3; the concern is he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: King David
runners_data.note: Blinkers on for Gay Kelleway, whose 0/1 recent record is slim but the headgear change is the key note; form in similar going is poor (3/15) with no wins or placed efforts, and on the figures alone this five-year-old looks exposed at this level over a mile on turf.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, King David nonetheless catches the eye here — our rating has him top of these nine on 65, and he has run over today's trip and going before, returning fit enough after just 13 days.

runners_data.name: Winemaker
runners_data.note: Runs in a hood for the in-form Richard Hughes yard (4/29 last 14 days, solid operator at this level); hold-up style means he needs a strong pace to get into contention, which today's single-pace-setter scenario does not guarantee, though the hood has appeared to help him settle better in recent runs.
runners_data.comment: Winemaker landed a win in his last six starts and that victory is backed by a speed rating of 67, while experience over today's trip and going holds him in good stead; the concern is that his two most recent runs have been a sixth and a seventh, leaving him with something to prove after a dip in form.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by nature — Billy Loughnane takes the ride — but the log-jam of similar types means he is unlikely to get as far back as he wants; he does hold course-and-distance winning form in similar going (3/7f GOO win), and Tony Carroll's yard (1/21 L14) provides modest confidence, though his natural race style is compromised in this shape.
runners_data.comment: River Wharfe arrives here in decent nick, third last time out and a winner two starts back, with experience of today's trip and going giving him every chance to go close again from stall 7; the main concern is his trainer's current lean spell.

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: Has won and placed multiple times over this course and distance in comparable ground, making her statistically the most course-fit runner here; she is a true rear-runner by inclination but finds herself operating in a busier midfield than ideal — Christian Howarth (3lb claim) could help carve a passage if the race bunches, and the Birkett yard has been placing horses well (2/7 L14).
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Heer's Sadie faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, with just ten days' rest keeping her fresh.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Courage
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago and that quick turnaround for a four-year-old warrants monitoring; naturally operates from the rear and will be crowded in today's midfield cluster, her best form over seven furlongs on good ground suggesting the step to a mile is a minor question mark, though three recent placed efforts show she is competitive at this grade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Chloe's Courage makes little appeal, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns quickly enough on six days' rest.

runners_data.name: Sangara
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has been dropped back from ten furlongs, which could bring improvement if the extra pace suits; form figures include a third over ten furlongs on soft and a fifth on good at this trip, but no wins and modest placings (0W0P in similar going) suggest she is holding her chance rather than threatening to outpace this field.
runners_data.comment: Sangara arrives here 19 days after a fifth, winless in her last five starts, though a third three starts back offers some encouragement; she has run over today's trip and going, but her official rating of 48 leaves her with plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Celtic John
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 42 days, which is a notable flag given the Pat Phelan yard is 2/6 recently — not a strong strike rate; hold-up style leaves him reliant on a strong pace he will not get, and his form at 8f on good ground is unremarkable (3/15 sim-going, 0W0P), making it hard to see him making a bold move.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Celtic John is hard to fancy; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 42 days between runs at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Monks Mead
runners_data.note: The race's sole pace-setter, wearing a hood, ridden by the Brighton-savvy Nicola Currie; the Style_Fit flag notes she is competing at a slightly higher OR than recent wins suggest she dominates at, but her uncontested lead role on Good to Firm ground over a flat mile is a significant tactical advantage that compensates for raw ability concerns.
runners_data.comment: Monks Mead has shown some consistency in recent starts, finishing third twice in his last six, though he remains winless and a winner has eluded him across that sequence; the drop to stall two and familiarity with today's trip and conditions offer encouragement, but his official mark of 45 leaves him needing to find more.

races.paceDynamic: Monks Mead is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, is set to dictate from the outset at a comfortable, controlled tempo over Brighton's undulating mile. Good to Firm ground (the actual going report overrides the declared Good) will keep the gallop honest but not searching, meaning Monks Mead can conserve energy through the middle portions before the home turn. That slow-to-moderate, front-dictated tempo classically favours horses who can travel prominently or at least in mid-division without having to make up excessive ground on a track where the straight is short and late closers can be left with nowhere to go. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — River Wharfe, Heer's Sadie, Chloe's Courage, Sangara and Celtic John are all natural rear-division horses who will be shuffled into an overcrowded midfield, with Heer's Sadie and River Wharfe — both proven at today's course and distance — most likely to actually find a workable position given their class advantage and jockey experience at Brighton.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Monks Mead Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead is allowed to bowl along in front at her own pace and no rival has the ability or inclination to challenge her before the turn.
scenarios.body: Monks Mead sets a measured tempo on Good to Firm ground, builds her lead into the short straight, and the fractured, midfield-clustered hold-up horses are left with too little track to reel her in; the Nicola Currie partnership knows Brighton well and will be alert to the challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Strike Through Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead's pace proves slightly too slow and the midfield becomes a wall, allowing a well-positioned hold-up type to find a seam and pounce.
scenarios.body: Heer's Sadie or River Wharfe, both proven over today's course and distance in similar ground, track closer than their natural style allows and arrive with enough momentum in the final furlong; the compressed midfield scenario actually suits horses quick enough to accelerate from a short distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead goes too fast for conditions and a prominent tracker such as one of the redistributed midfielders hustles up to join her earlier than anticipated.
scenarios.body: The front end fragments as the home turn arrives, giving a well-handicapped hold-up type who has sat just off the pace — most plausibly Chloe's Courage or Heer's Sadie — a gap to fill through tired horses in the final stages; the short Brighton straight limits how many can benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Cuts Through Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded midfield causes interference or traffic problems, and a wide-travelling runner bypasses the trouble to emerge late.
scenarios.body: Dalmally or Winemaker, both natural hold-up types with straightforward recent form over the mile, manage to find clear air by racing wide while the interior becomes congested; with modest ORs and accessible weights, either could capitalise if the pace scenario plays into their hands.

watchPoints.text: Monks Mead (Nicola Currie) is uncontested in front — watch her stride pattern between the half-mile and quarter-mile marks; if she is not being ridden, the lead is almost certainly building to a winning margin the closers cannot reel in.

The midfield is dangerously crowded with five natural hold-up horses (River Wharfe, Heer's Sadie, Chloe's Courage, Sangara, Celtic John) all forced to compete for the same ground — watch for early jostling and positional delays that could cost any of them vital lengths entering the short straight.

Heer's Sadie and River Wharfe both carry strong course-and-distance credentials but are racing out of their ideal position; if either can tuck in behind Monks Mead from the outset rather than sitting deep in the pack, their chance improves materially — watch the first two furlongs for signs of a positive break.

Good to Firm going (the actual track condition, confirmed by the going report) is noticeably faster than the declared Good — horses with previous form on Firm or Fast surfaces, and those who travel well on quick ground, may be subtly advantaged over those whose best form has come on softer surfaces.

Chloe's Courage ran only six days ago; watch for any sign of sluggishness or a flat warm-up, which on such a quick turnaround would suggest she has not fully recovered, and adjust her chance accordingly before the off.

races.name: Brighton Racecourse Antiques And Vintage Fair Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kondratiev Wave
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who maps as the lone pace-setter here and will enjoy an uncontested lead; OR 55 with Billy Loughnane up for Tony Carroll, though 18 days off and a flat sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 on similar ground tempers confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Kondratiev Wave has run over today's trip and going, and his recent form includes a second two starts back and a second five starts back, giving him solid each-way claims here; the main risk is a trainer firing at just 5% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Berning Hot
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type for William Carson and Michael Attwater, who has posted a win from 15 similar-going runs and was second over 8f on Good recently — stretching slightly back to 7f but has proven form at the trip; genuine closer who needs gaps.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Berning Hot showed encouragement with a second four starts back but has been below that level since, posting a fifth last time out after 19 days off; she has run over today's trip and going, though 133 lb from stall seven is no straightforward task.

runners_data.name: Thanks Dad
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon-trained six-year-old wearing a visor, ran just ten days ago, and scored over 6f on Good; steps up to 7f here and is a natural hold-up runner who will need to deliver later than ideal given the modest pace likely to be set.|
runners_data.comment: Thanks Dad won last time out, which catches the eye, but that single victory in his last five starts is surrounded by poor efforts, and he rates well below most rivals on our figures, ranked seventh of nine.

runners_data.name: Mister Sandman
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore four-year-old in hood who is a confirmed hold-up horse by nature, but the glut of closers in this field forces him into a midfield map slot he won't naturally seek — 0W2P from 13 similar-going runs gives a fair baseline, and Jude Fernandes claims 7lb.|
runners_data.comment: Mister Sandman is the top-rated runner in the field and has experience of today's trip and conditions, showing consistent placing ability with a second two starts back; yet to score in his last five starts, and that lack of a win remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes three-year-old wearing a visor, who recorded a win over 7f on Good and ran 17 days ago; hold-up profile that is genuine rather than redistributed and arrives on a form line that includes a recent flat-track win — going and trip appear squarely in range.|
runners_data.comment: Superstorm shaped as a strong contender here, returning off a confident 17-day break as a winner last time out and carrying experience of today's trip and conditions into the race from stall one; the risk is that his form in the five starts prior to that win was inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Barry The Worm
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne three-year-old in blinkers who is a true hold-up runner by history but finds himself mapped into midfield due to the field's cluster of closers; 0W0P from 11 similar-going runs and a recent string of poor finishes make his chances slim regardless of traffic.|
runners_data.comment: Barry The Worm won five starts back but has been well held in three of his four most recent efforts, and while he has run over today's trip and going and returns on a reasonable 27-day break from stall 5, an official mark of 52 leaves little room to enthuse.

runners_data.name: Neat And Tidy
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes three-year-old with a 4/29 T14 strike rate, who has gone winless and placeless in six similar-going runs; a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by the packed rear-of-field, and a form string of 59-055 offers little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Neat And Tidy returns on a quick turnaround of 14 days and has run over today's trip and going, giving her experience of the conditions. Winless in her last five starts, but our rating of 57 edges above her official mark, making her interesting from stall six.

runners_data.name: Girls Allowed
runners_data.note: Julia & Shelley Birkett three-year-old with a prominent profile and a course-relevant second over 7f on Good recently — the only runner likely to shadow Kondratiev Wave and the main beneficiary if the race is truly run to suit the prominent shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Girls Allowed faces a stiff ask here, though she does bring distance and going experience to the table and a return run 22 days ago suggests she is fit enough.

runners_data.name: Nautical Sky
runners_data.note: James Owen three-year-old with a strong T14 trainer in form (6/42), returning after 48 days off; a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield map berth by the field's density of closers, and a p/h headgear note suggests he sits handy — worth monitoring if freshened by the break.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a seventh last time out and a return to form as a second three starts back not enough to inspire confidence here; she has run over today's trip and is drawn in stall four, but our figures rank her eighth of nine.

races.paceDynamic: Kondratiev Wave is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 7f Brighton handicap and, with no other horse genuinely expected to contest the lead, will enjoy an uncontested, pressure-free passage from the outset. Girls Allowed is the only other prominent-style runner and is unlikely to seriously challenge for the front, meaning Kondratiev Wave can dictate tempo entirely on its own terms on ground that is Good to Firm throughout the card. The remainder of the field — Berning Hot, Thanks Dad, Superstorm, and genuinely held-up types Mister Sandman, Barry The Worm, Neat And Tidy, and Nautical Sky — will be chasing from off the pace, but the field holds significantly more hold-up types than can all find their natural rear position; Mister Sandman, Barry The Worm, Neat And Tidy, and Nautical Sky are redistributed into midfield slots they will not naturally want, meaning effective early separation in the pack behind will be limited. On fast ground at Brighton with a single front-runner setting a controlled, sustainable gallop, this race shape heavily favours the prominent/lead profile — a horse that can travel close to Kondratiev Wave and pounce entering the final two furlongs without being embroiled in the bunched midfield traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kondratiev Wave Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave sets a true solo lead at a sustainable pace and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Kondratiev Wave controls every yard, and on fast Brighton ground with no pressure applied, a measured gallop means the lead is never surrendered; Girls Allowed, the only other prominent runner, is best placed to track and challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Stride Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Girls Allowed tracks Kondratiev Wave closely and the two pull clear of a bunched midfield pack.
scenarios.body: The genuine prominent runners exploit the gap opened by the solo pace-setter and the compression behind them; the hold-up horses, forced into unnatural midfield berths, cannot find clear runs quickly enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave sets a genuinely fast fractions and ties up in the final furlong, leaving room for a well-timed closer.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse that finds a clear run through the redistributed midfield traffic could pick up the pieces; Superstorm and Berning Hot, with genuine hold-up profiles and course-relevant going stats, are best suited to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble, Chaos Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed midfield group creates sustained traffic and interference, producing a messy finish with no clean winner.
scenarios.body: Horses forced out of role block each other's runs, the pace collapses into a messy bunch finish, and the winner emerges from whichever runner finds the clearest passage soonest; Thanks Dad or Mister Sandman could benefit from a gap.

watchPoints.text: Kondratiev Wave's ability to control the fractions unchallenged is the single biggest determinant of this race — if Billy Loughnane elects a slow early pace, he could prove extremely difficult to peg back on Good to Firm Brighton ground.

Girls Allowed is the only other prominent-profile runner and Dylan Hogan should be able to slot in directly behind Kondratiev Wave; if she tracks the leader throughout, she is best placed to strike if the leader weakens, giving her significant positional advantage over the field.

Mister Sandman, Barry The Worm, Neat And Tidy, and Nautical Sky are all true hold-up horses forced into midfield — watch for a bunched group entering the straight where traffic incidents are likely and multiple runners may find their runs blocked simultaneously.

Superstorm (visor, Charlie Fellowes, recent win on Good over 7f) is the hold-up runner with the most credible recent form and going profile — watch whether Mikkel Mortensen (5lb claimer) can find a clean passage down the outside if the midfield compresses.

Nautical Sky returns after 48 days off for in-form trainer James Owen (T14: 6/42) — a freshened horse from a yard in good form can sometimes outrun a flat recent form string, and Cieren Fallon's booking is a notable upgrade in class of jockey.
